messages:
Nina (PM): dropping a quick thread: deciding between inline helper chips vs modal overlay for first-run guidance. fig: https://www.figma.com/file/qrst2345/onboard-helper

Rosa (Designer): inline chips feel lighter and keep context, overlay is more discoverable and supports step-by-step. chips can expand into a small panel.

Cal (Frontend): inline is easier to keep in DOM flow and less likely to cause scroll jumps. overlay needs focus trap and background inert. both need persisted dismissed state.

Ivy (Research): users in our last study found overlays interruptive but highly effective for low-discovery features. chips had good retention but lower activation. suggestion: test overlay for brand-new workspaces, chips for returning users.

Tom (A11y): accessibility notes:
- overlay must set aria-hidden on background and focus the first interactive element inside the dialog
- inline chips must be keyboard reachable and have aria-expanded states when they surface more content
- both need clear labels; avoid "Got it" alone for close buttons (use "Dismiss onboarding" for screen readers)

Sam (Devex): analytics: event onboarding_ui=chip|overlay, onboarding_step, shown_at, interacted, dismissed_reason. add experiment_id.

Rosa (Designer): copy options: "Try a sample project" vs "Walkthrough: Get started". chips could show microcopy: "5 min to try the Chat demo".

Nina (PM): proposal: show overlay for 20% new workspaces for the initial run, chips for the rest. include a short intercept survey on dismiss to capture "too pushy" feedback.

Cal (Frontend): implementation checklist: persist state per workspace, feature-flag rollout, ensure no scroll-lock regressions on mobile. will prototype overlay variant with role=dialog and inert polyfill.

Tom (A11y): also recommend adding aria-live polite announcement when chip expands so screen reader users know new content appeared. and ensure color tokens for contrast.

Ivy (Research): can run 10 moderated sessions on overlay vs chip in the canary cohort to capture qualitative reactions.

product-bot: reminder: run axe smoke + keyboard-nav tests on PRs.

Nina (PM): actions: Rosa post updated frames with both variants + contrast numbers; Cal PR for chip + overlay baseline; Sam add events and flag; Tom review a11y; Ivy schedule quick sessions. target: Fri EOD for prototypes. :thumbsup:

Rosa (Designer): on it  will include microcopy variants and mobile behavior.

Nina (PM): thanks team, will follow up with rollout plan once we have initial metrics.
